rows.grounds: refers to persons unable to speak
compound denoting persons both deaf and mute; analyzed as fused form
instrument indicating the means of expressing assent
written sign serving as an alternative means of assent

items.question: By what means can mute and deaf-mute witnesses convey valid assent?
premises: Mute persons cannot convey assent through spoken words.
Deaf-mute persons likewise lack ordinary verbal expression.
A nod of the head or writing can communicate agreement.
items.inference: Therefore, for mute and deaf-mute witnesses, assent is conveyed by a nod of the head or by writing.
uncertainties: The exact evidentiary status of such assent in this context depends on the preceding discussion of witness testimony.
items.plain_english: For mute and deaf-mute persons, assent is expressed by a nod of the head or by writing.
